title: Transparent rate mirroring and ordered failover for tenant surge protection
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: After the February outage (see postmortem link in comments) we observed two problematic behaviors during cross-region congestion: 1) abrupt local limiter outages causing asymmetric shedding across regions and 2) loss of request ordering at the admission layer which amplified tail latency for long-running chat sessions. This ticket proposes a mid-term runtime feature called 'transparent rate mirroring' plus an 'ordered failover' policy to improve SLO stability, reduce unfairness across tenants, and make limiter outages gracefully degradable.
goal: Provide an SLO-driven admission gateway that mirrors tenant credit state to a standby region in a compact, append-only stream and performs an ordered failover that preserves per-tenant fairness and session ordering when local limiter instances are degraded or Blackout. Reduce 99th percentile latency SLO breaches caused by admission rejections during cross-region incidents by >= 60% in our simulated scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end e2e simulation reproduces previous outage pattern and shows 60% fewer SLO violations at p99 for affected tenants. 2) Failover switchover completes within configured window (default 6s) with preserved request ordering for active session tokens. 3) No additional p50 latency regression (>3%) in normal operation. 4) Dashboard exposes mirrored-credit lag, failover count, and fairness score. 5) Rollout gating: canary in us-west-2 at 5% of traffic with automatic rollback on >3% increase in errors.
design_notes: - Mirror format: compact delta stream of tenant credits (lease-ish units) with sequence numbers and tombstones for revokes. Use protobuf + zstd and append to an S3-backed replication log for infrequent large state syncs. - Mirroring frequency: adaptive; base cadence 1s with backpressure-aware coalescing. - Ordered failover: when local admission detects unavailable limiter (heartbeat timeout or OOM kill), it transitions to 'proxy-standby' mode where requests are routed to local acceptor only if sequence check passes. A deterministic per-session affinity token ensures requests are ordered to the same acceptor until eviction. - Fairness preservation: on failover, we replay mirrored credits for the tenant in the standby region and apply exponential credit decay to avoid burst amplification. - Circuit breaker interactions: integrate with existing circuit state machine (CB-open => trigger ordered failover earlier for affected tenants). - Trade-offs: extra network IO and storage overhead for mirroring vs faster recovery and fairness guarantees. We mitigate cost by sampling and only mirroring tenants above a burst threshold and by delta compression.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (prototype): mirror stream producer at admission layer + lightweight consumer that validates sequence numbers (2 weeks). Phase 2 (simulator): build offline simulator that can inject regional latency/oos and measure SLOs with/without mirroring (2 weeks). Phase 3 (canary): enable read-only mirroring in us-west-2 routing 5% traffic, collect metrics, iterate (2 weeks). Phase 4 (failover enable): enable ordered failover with automatic rollback guards + gradual ramp (2 weeks).
testing_and_simulation: - Add deterministic simulator tests to chaos-suite that inject network partitions and limiter process restarts. - Create tenant-shaped traffic patterns from production traces (sampled) to evaluate fairness metrics (Gini coefficient of accepted tokens across tenants). - Run regional outage replay in staging with 1000+ concurrent sessions and validate ordering and credit preservation. - Performance microbench: measure mirror write latency (target <3ms median).
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboard widgets: mirrored-lag-ms, mirror-error-rate, failover-count, per-tenant fairness-score, p99 latency delta (canary vs baseline). Alerts: >5s median mirrored-lag for >1m, failover-rate > 1/min sustained for 5m, canary p99 latency >+3% vs baseline for 10m. Post-deploy runbook: steps to roll back canary, how to force-evict mirrored state, and how to rehydrate after outage.
rollout_strategy: Canary in single region (us-west-2) with 5% traffic, 24h soak. If canary passes, ramp to 30% across two regions, then global. Automatic rollback conditions: canary p99 > +3% or error increase >1% absolute. Manual rollback: toggle feature flag in console and drain in-flight mirrored state.
notes: We intentionally avoid synchronous cross-region coordination on the critical path; mirroring is best-effort and used for graceful failover only. For regulated customers requiring strict isolation, mirroring will be opt-in and limited to intra-VPC/private deployments.
comments: 2026-02-12 Aisha: Created ticket after postmortem. Initial architecture sketch attached. Marked P0 due to customer impact on enterprise rolling updates.

2026-02-18 Miguel: Prototype for compact mirror encoding done; pushed draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892. Notable: protobuf layout needs field for 'session-affinity-token' to preserve ordering.
2026-02-25 Liang Chen (review): Suggested adaptive cadence and sampling policy. Concerned about memory growth in high-tenant-count hosts — proposed tombstone compaction pass.
2026-03-02 SRE: Ran first simulator run; reproduced outage pattern. Mirroring reduced p99 SLO breaches by 48% in baseline run; need further tuning on decay constant to hit 60% goal.
2026-03-07 Product (Rina Kapoor): Approved acceptance criteria. Request to expose per-tenant 'failover-score' in Console for enterprise transparency.
2026-03-10 Miguel: Implemented ordered failover state machine and added unit tests for sequence monotonicity. Preparing canary plan and manifest. Next: load test for mirror write overhead.
sim_results: 2026-03-02: baseline replay: 124 p99 SLO breaches across 1000 tenants
2026-03-02: with mirroring: 64 p99 SLO breaches (48% reduction)
2026-03-05: tuned decay constant: 78 breaches (37% reduction) — indicates need for smarter per-tenant decay
operational_playbook: If failover is triggered unexpectedly: 1) Mark region as degraded in Console and enable manual rollback. 2) If mirrored-lag > 10s, pause mirroring producers and allow consumer to catch up. 3) Force-consume compact snapshot to rehydrate in-memory credits. 4) Open incident and escalate to runtime on-call. Include command snippets in Confluence playbook link.
customer_communication: Template drafted for customers impacted by cross-region admission disruptions. Will include expected behavior, opt-out for mirroring, and timeline for canary. Targeted outreach for enterprise customers with reserved capacity.
next_steps: Finish load-test and quantify mirror write CPU/latency overhead
Add admin APIs to inspect mirrored window and evict per-tenant state
Enable canary in us-west-2 and monitor soaks for 48h
